item.title: The Art of System Hacking: Mindset Over Tools
item.description:
TL;DR: Hacking systems isn’t about tools—it’s about understanding how things fit together.

The Three-Layer Model

Every system (technical or social) breaks down into three layers:

  1. The Visible Layer - What you see on the surface. APIs, UIs, documented procedures.
  2. The Structural Layer - How components connect. Network topology, permissions, trust relationships.
  3. The Assumption Layer - What the designers believed would never happen.

The hack always lives in the gap between the Structural and Assumption layers.

Practical Exercise

Next time you’re trying to “get into” something (a system, an organization, a codebase), map these three layers on paper before firing up Burp or writing a script.

You’ll find the attack surface shrinks dramatically—and the paths become obvious.

Posted from the command line. No GUI. All business.

item.title: Bash One-Liners That Feel Illegal to Know
item.description:
Bash isn’t just a shell—it’s a Glasstype of Swiss Army knife that’s been lying in your terminal this whole time.

Process monitoring with ps in one line 

1ps aux | awk '{print $2, $3, $11}' | sort -k2r | head -10

Shows top 10 processes by CPU, with just PID, %CPU, and command. Clean.

Find and delete empty directories recursively (safely) 

1find . -type d -empty -delete

That’s it. No rm -rf confirmation theater. Just clean removal.

Watch a log file, but only the juicy parts 

1tail -f /var/log/syslog | grep --line-buffered -E 'ERROR|WARN|CRIT'

Real-time filtering. Because your eyes aren’t regex parsers.

pv — the unsung hero

Install pv (pipe viewer) and watch your data flow:

1cat huge-file.txt | pv -l | wc -l

Shows progress as lines pass through. Feels like cheating.

Protip: These aren’t hacks—they’re just bash doing what it was designed to do. Most people never read the manual.
